description: Penalty-constant sensitivity of the paper's regret contrasts, repriced from the retained decisions of the authors' frozen archive. Frozen rules: route cost = latency_EWMA + P x failure_rate + P x [circuit=OPEN]; observable-best re-selected under the same P for every decision; the wait rule is NOT rescaled (wait regret = 500 + 10,000 - best_P). Completion counts come from recorded outcomes and do not depend on P.
notes: Study 1 B-to-C reduction: 96.9% at P=10,000 -> 89.8% at 5,000 -> 67.8% at 1,000; about 29 percentage points of the headline are penalty pricing, the majority of the contrast survives all three pricings.

Study 1 arm C mean regret RISES as P falls (131.12 -> 256.12 -> 356.12 ms): C's entire residual regret is its 3 wait decisions, scored by the frozen wait rule 10,500 - best_P, which grows as best_P shrinks.

Study 2 arm C is exactly 0 at all three pricings, so the percentage reduction is degenerate (100% throughout, uninformative); the absolute B-C gap is reported instead: 8,956.37 -> 4,511.92 -> 956.37 ms.
